context: cleanroom factory · sub-fab utilities, ultra-pure systems and tool hook-up; cleanroom certification gates everything

brief.intro: New to this project type? A semiconductor fab is a cleanroom wrapped in utilities. Chips are made on silicon wafers by hundreds of process tools, in air thousands of times cleaner than an operating theatre. The building is a sandwich: above the cleanroom, fans and filters push clean air down; below it, a sub-fab holds the pumps, pipes and cables that serve every tool through the raised floor. Around it are plants for ultra-pure water, bulk and specialty gases, chemicals, exhaust treatment and wastewater. The structure must barely vibrate. After the shell is built, work is done under a strict clean protocol; then each tool is moved in, 'hooked up' to twenty or more services, and qualified. Tool hook-up is a project as large as the building.

must_get_right: The schedule has three gates: building weather-tight, cleanroom certified, and tools hooked up. Nothing in a later gate may start before the earlier one is passed.
Utility systems (UPW, gases, chemicals, exhaust) are high-purity installations with their own testing and certification; they need as much time as the building.
Tool hook-up is hundreds of small projects; plan it tool by tool against the tool delivery schedule, with design, prefabrication, installation and sign-off for each.
Vibration, cleanliness and life-safety (toxic gas) requirements are acceptance criteria — failures at certification cost months.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by plant area along the process line and by discipline, with every long-lead machine tracked from order to factory test, shipping and arrival.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar until the building is enclosed; hook-up and qualification usually run two or three shifts. Clean-protocol work is slower and is planned with reduced productivity.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Structure and waffle slab → building weather-tight → cleanroom build under clean protocol → facility systems → cleanroom certification → tool move-in → hook-up → qualification → first silicon. Utility plants are built in parallel and must be certified before hook-up. The critical path runs through the cleanroom certification and then the tool delivery / hook-up sequence.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The process technology and vendor are fixed before design starts; vendor drawings for foundations arrive on the agreed dates; permanent power and water are available before cold commissioning; raw material for trial production is on site.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule tracks the following as milestones because they drive the programme:

rows: Fan-filter units, raised floor & cleanroom systems

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy machines need crane access and often must enter before the cladding or a wall is closed. Vendor supervisors are booked for fixed periods. Clean, dry, powered conditions are required before precision equipment is unpacked.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: failed cleanroom or vibration certification, purity failures in gas and water lines, late tools, hook-up design lagging tool arrival, and a long yield ramp. Contingency is held before tool move-in and before first silicon.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by plant area and discipline; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the installation crews and the vendor supervisors — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
